exposure: mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal, assisted vaginal, cesarean)
outcome: coexistence of craniosynostosis and ossified cephalhematomas
cohort: The study included craniosynostosis cases treated at a large children's hospital from November 2007 through September 2021, with a specific focus on 75 patients with ossified cephalhematomas.
finding: In this series, 9.3% of ossified cephalhematoma cases had coexisting craniosynostosis, demonstrating a rare association between the two conditions, though its nature remains elusive.
